area: Client Connector, the rest of the way (zcc_bypass.py and the Path analyzer's Client Connector step, the profile builder's tamper passwords in ops_zcc.py, one device's one-time passwords in zcc_otp.py and /api/zcc/otp)
title: Every Client Connector bypass evaluated on the path with the list that decided named; tamper passwords typed, sent once and never kept; device one-time passwords as a gated, rate-limited, audited read that keeps nothing

checks.what: Oracle tables for the Client Connector step: VPN gateway bypass (host, wildcard, address, address with a port, none), IP-based application bypass (custom, predefined by id and appSvcId, app service id; address, port range, protocol, fqdn), Z-Tunnel 1.0 and Tunnel with local proxy (TCP 80 and 443 only), Enforce proxy (web only), Z-Tunnel 2.0 (every port; exclusions, limited inclusions), each naming the list and entry that decided

Unknowns stay unknown: IP-based application definitions that cannot be read leave an address unknown (verdict 'Unable to verify how the device reaches', also for traffic that is not web), limited Z-Tunnel 2.0 inclusions leave a host name unknown, the Z-Tunnel 1.0 proxy-port option leaves another web port unknown

Tamper passwords: preview shows set (hidden); the plan hash covers a salted, keyed digest (a different password or salt moves it, plan_changed writes nothing); sent once in the create call (Windows snake-case and macOS camel-case SDK fields); read back as set without the value; a read-back without the field is not confirmed
checks.standard: ASVS V8.3.4 · ASVS V11.1.1 · CWE-256 · CWE-345

checks.what: No sink holds a password in any encoding (typed, URL, form, JSON, a fragment): plan, plan PDF, approval request, job result and log, record, audit log, console, and errors that echo the request body (an error answer, an exception, ZCC's success false) all masked

Passwords are taken only by the profile builder, validated before sign-in (known fields, at most 128 characters, no control characters) without echoing a value, and must be typed again for the apply; the page keeps them out of the spec and of browser storage
checks.standard: ASVS V5.1.3 · ASVS V8.2.2 · CWE-20 · CWE-922

checks.what: Device one-time passwords: scope (checked first), a person who may change the tenant, the named assessor (not the tool), SHOW OTP <device> typed, the device validated, all before sign-in; at most 5 a person in 10 minutes and 30 in an hour (429 with Retry-After, audited)
checks.standard: ASVS V4.1.1 · ASVS V4.1.3 · ASVS V11.1.4 · CWE-285 · CWE-799 · WSTG-ATHZ-02

checks.what: Device one-time passwords are in the answer only (no-store, no-cache); the audit entry names who, the assessor, the device (host name and UDID hash) and the kinds shown, never a value; an unknown or ambiguous device shows nothing and is audited; the page hides them after 60 seconds or on Hide now and stores nothing
checks.standard: ASVS V8.3.4 · CWE-524 · CWE-532 · WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.1

findings.title: The Path analyzer read the app profile's VPN gateways and IP-based application ids but never evaluated them: a VPN gateway or an IP-based app bypass was reported as reaching Zscaler
findings.fix: zcc_bypass.py: VPN gateway check, IP-based application definitions read (SDK custom-ip-based-apps, predefined-ip-based-apps, webAppService) and matched by address, host name, port and protocol; data_flow.trace names the deciding list; Test a list indexes the new lists

findings.title: Z-Tunnel 1.0 carried every web port in the trace (TCP 8080 and 8443 included), and a host name that limited Z-Tunnel 2.0 inclusions would need resolved was reported as tunnelled
findings.fix: zcc_bypass.tunnel_check (TCP 80 and 443 for Z-Tunnel 1.0, unknown with the proxy-port option) and tunnel2_lists (unknown for a host name with limited inclusions)

findings.title: For traffic that is not web, an unverified Client Connector or forwarding step still ended in the firewall's headline and a 'blind' outcome
findings.fix: zia_path_modules.extend_trace keeps 'unknown' and annotate_verdict keeps 'Unable to verify how the device reaches' (the firewall's decision moves to the summary, as what applies if the traffic gets there)
